Made-with: Cursor

Crash-proof: guarantee terminal cleanup and catch panics

- Wrap TUI event loop in catch_unwind so terminal is always restored
  to normal mode even on panics or errors (no more broken terminal)
- Wrap thread::scope init spawns with catch_unwind to prevent
  propagation of panics from hardware probe functions
- Handle --dump IOReport failure with user-friendly error message
  instead of raw anyhow error

Add Display, Camera, PCIe, Media Engine, Fabric from IOReport

ignored, adding real measured power data for:

- Camera ISP
- PCIe/Thunderbolt ports
- Media Engine (AVE + MSR)
- Fabric interconnect (AMCC + DCS + FAB + AFR)

These appear as new rows under the SoC node in the power tree,
with SMA smoothing, Wh totals, and sparkline history.

Fix heap buffer overflow in proc_pid_rusage and harden FFI safety

Critical: rusage_info_v4 buffer was 8 bytes too small (288 vs 296),
causing kernel to write past the heap allocation on every PID scan.
Also fixed wrong field offset: was reading ri_cycles (offset 256)
instead of ri_billed_energy (offset 264).

Additional safety:
- Null check after host_processor_info success
- IORegistryEntryGetName return code checks + null-terminate buffers

Add multi-die Apple Silicon support, Ethernet detection, WiFi interface fix

- Generic DIE_N_ prefix stripping for multi-die chips (M1/M2/M3 Ultra)

- Extended parse_cpu_stats_core_key with ACC-style fallback for _CPU suffix

- Changed 5 exact block power name matches (ISP, DISP, DISPEXT, AVE|MSR,
  AMCC|DCS|FAB|AFR) to starts_with for forward-compatible per-die suffixes
- Added Ethernet detection via getifaddrs (IFT_ETHER, link speed, interface name)
- Fixed WiFi SSID detection: get interface name from CWInterface.interfaceName
  instead of hardcoded en0 (Mac Studio has WiFi on en1, not en0)
- WiFi shows "(off)" instead of "(scanning...)" when no WiFi hardware present
- Guarded CPU avg usage against NaN from division by zero (0 cores detected)
- Added IOReport channel naming documentation to README

- Ethernet and WiFi collapsible with Download/Upload children, collapsed by default
- No fake power estimates for Ethernet (already counted in SoC/PCIe)

Universal CPU temperature mapping with stale value caching

Replace hardcoded single-die temperature patterns with a universal
bank-based algorithm that works across all Apple Silicon generations
(M1-M5+, including Ultra dual-die chips).

Key changes:
- SMC temp keys parsed as T{type}{bank}{suffix} using base-62 alphabet
- Bank encoding: die*5 + cluster_offset ('0'-'4' = die 0, '5'-'9' = die 1)
- Direct bank selection instead of fragile exact-count matching
- Primary Tp0 bank fallback for chips without Te keys (M5 Max)
- Stale value caching in SMC reader: sensors that temporarily fail
  show last known value with ~ prefix (e.g. ~37°C)
- 11 unit tests covering single-die, dual-die Ultra, M5 Max primary
  bank, partial sensor loss, stale flag propagation, and legacy fallback
- README updated with UI legend explaining all symbols and indicators

refactor: harden sampler lifecycle and command execution

Make background data sources shut down cleanly and tighten IOReport resource cleanup to avoid detached threads and native handle leaks. Add command timeouts, stricter nettop parsing, CI-safe unit-test execution, and clearer library/CLI boundaries to improve reliability and maintainability.

fix: avoid Dock flashing in EDR probe

Stop calling NSApplication sharedApplication in the periodic Python EDR subprocess, since that marks the process as a GUI app and causes Dock icon flashing. Keep EDR sampling resilient by falling back to NSScreen.screens().firstObject and returning 1.0 when no screen is available.

Made-with: Cursor

fix(smc): handle Mac Neo display backlight key (PBwo) + add --dump-smc

Issue #12: on MacBook Neo (M5 Pro/Max generation) `PDBR` no longer reflects
backlight power; the new key `PBwo` does. Read PBwo first and fall back to
PDBR so older Macs (M1-M4 XDR) keep the existing behavior.

Also:
- Make SmcConnection::read_key_raw return Err when SMC reports
  data_size=0/data_type=0 (kernel returns kr=0 for unknown keys but with
  empty info — previously surfaced as a silent Ok(0.0) from read_f32 and
  defeated any or_else fallback).
- Add SmcConnection::dump_all and a new --dump-smc CLI flag that emits every
  SMC key in iSMC raw format (KEY [type] decoded (bytes hex)) so users on
  unfamiliar hardware can attach a triage dump to issues.
- Verified on M5 Max (Mac17,7): PBwo absent → falls through to PDBR; on
  Mac Neo per the issue reporter PBwo is present and tracks brightness.

rm release notes

fix(display): replace Python EDR probe with in-process CoreDisplay (#9)

The periodic Python+ctypes subprocess that read NSScreen's EDR headroom
caused a "Python" icon to flash in the Dock every few seconds (issue #9):
loading AppKit registers the helper as a GUI process even with the
NSApplication-avoidance trick, and `setActivationPolicy:Prohibited` only
papered over part of it. The deeper problem was that we were extracting
real-time display state from the wrong API.

Yellow/integral fix: drop the AppKit subprocess entirely and source
display state from APIs that already publish it live, in-process:

- Reference Mode (the user's current preset, e.g. "Apple XDR Display
  (P3-1600 nits)") via private CoreDisplay framework:
  `CoreDisplay_Display_GetActivePresetIndex` + `_CopyPreset`. Updates
  immediately when the user changes the preset in System Settings →
  Displays. No NSApplication, no AppKit init, no Dock flashing.
- Refresh rate / ProMotion via `CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode` and
  `CGDisplayCopyAllDisplayModes`.
- HDR-active state from IOReport's "backlight report" group, channel
  `DPB factor` (Display Power Boost, 16.16 fixed-point — `>1.0` means
  HDR pipeline is currently engaged).
- Panel class (SDR / HDR / XDR) from `BrightnessMilliNits.max`
  thresholds as a fallback when the preset API returns nothing.

The display label now reads e.g.
`14" · Apple XDR Display · 1600/1600 nits · 120Hz` and updates as the
slider moves and the user switches presets. Current nits is
`slider × preset peak nits`, matching System Settings's mental model
(slider 100% in P3-1600 = 1600 nits, in P3-600 = 600 nits).

Also drops the python3 runtime dependency and the ~50-line ctypes
script that came with it.

Verified on M5 Max (Mac17,7): no Python child process, no Dock
flashing, all 17 tests pass (1 new for `short_preset_name`).

Bump version to 0.1.19

Pin toolchain via rust-toolchain.toml so local clippy/fmt match CI's
`stable` and we don't ship a release that locally-old clippy approves
but newer-stable CI rejects (this is what happened to v0.1.18, where
`clippy::collapsible_match` was promoted to a default warning in 1.95
and tripped CI after `cargo publish` had already locked the version).

Also tightens the README release checklist: rustup update first,
copy the clippy command verbatim from .github/workflows/ci.yml,
dry-run publish before tagging, and don't try to force-push tags
once cargo publish has happened — yank + bump instead.

Fixes the actual lint in src/main.rs by collapsing the inner
`if app.handle_key(key)` into the match guard.
